kxexe01.title: Why does the Moon follow my car?
kxexe01.caption:
Drove home from my ex's and the Moon followed me the whole way.
It's so far away its direction barely changes, so it seems to keep pace. Big feelings work the same: let them ride along, and they set.

kxexe02.title: Is the Moon leaving us?
kxexe02.caption:
No fight. We just stopped texting.
The Moon drifts about 3.8 cm a year, and most friendships drift just as quietly. The pull back is small too: one text.

kxexe03.title: Why do stars twinkle but planets don't?
kxexe03.caption:
Sparkly one week, gone the next.
Stars twinkle because of the moving air between us, not the star. Mixed signals are often static too: skip the guessing and ask one clear question.

kxexe04.title: Is the North Star the brightest star?
kxexe04.caption:
Plot twist: the North Star isn't the brightest one up there.
It's famous because it stays put while the whole sky turns. Keep the people you can find in the dark.

kxexe05.title: Why can't I see my sign on my birthday?
kxexe05.caption:
Looked up on my birthday and my sign wasn't even there.
The Sun is parked in front of it all day. If you want a fuss, say so out loud: people can't read the sky in your head.

kxexe06.title: Why do shooting stars come back every December?
kxexe06.caption:
Wished on every shooting star that they'd text me.
Each December Earth crosses the same trail of space dust. A wish is a lovely start; the brave, kind part is texting first.
